title.narrative: Enhancing access to multi-sectoral life-saving and essential humanitarian assistance to war-affected newly displaced and non-displaced people living near the frontline in Ukraine.

description.narrative: ltpgtUnder this project a consortium of UK-Med and partner CO «100 PERCENT LIFE» DNIPROV REGION" (100% LIFE) propose to implement a multisectoral and complementary intervention in the most critical areas of need - Protection and Health. The proposed action aligns with the priorities outlined in the call for proposal and outlined by the 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response plan (HNRP). The Consortium will work together on project with title: Enhancing access to multi-sectoral lifesaving and essential humanitarian assistance to newly placed internally displaced, non-displaced people living close to the frontline and affected by the war in Ukraine. The activities would be in Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. The project has 2 Health and 2 Protection outcomes, and the following is a summary of the key activities: ltbrgt ltbrgt1. Provision of lifesaving and essential health services to vulnerable populations affected by war ltbrgt ltbrgt Case management and provision of quality health services to IDPs and non- IDP people in the project areas (include MHPSS, RCCE, Referrals, Identification for PWDs, provision of critical donations) ltbrgt Working with IDP collection centers ltbrgt Training community members on First AID and Psychological first aid to build personal/community resilience to acute shocks and lifesaving skills ltbrgt Training health care workers in different disciplines: focus on PHC providers (NCD training, mhGAP) and Hospital and Emergency department on trauma. ltbrgt Provision of Donations to PHC facilities (medicines and equipment). ltbrgt Provision of support to health care workers address stress and burnout (care for carers – C4C), two workshops are proposed. ltbrgt Provision of Cash Voucher assistance to access transport (minimizing barriers to access health) ltbrgt ltbrgt2. To improve access to health services through emergency preparedness of affected communities. ltbrgt Training trauma hospital staff on Mass Casualty Incidence management (MCI) ltbrgt ltbrgt ltbrgt3. Improve access to inclusive protection services ltbrgt ltbrgtProtection case management to include counselling, legal support ltbrgtProtection Cash support to access food assistance and assistive technologies for PWDs ltbrgtDonations of kits (hygiene, dignity kits) ltbrgtTransport service (CVA) protection to access referral and other services ltbrgt4. Strengthening protection environment and capacity of service provider ltbrgt ltbrgtWorkshop with local protection actors (state and non-state) at oblast level to discuss protection services access. ltbrgtKey cross cutting issues would also be addressed across the proposed action: Gender age consideration, accountability of affected populations (AAP) and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
